title: Employee Scheduling Solution v3.0
description: The output half of a package: problem + optional solution -> algorithm -> package. Records which daily working assignment each worker took on each day [x_wdh = 1]. Serves two roles with one shape: a FULL solution (every worker-day stated) and a PARTIAL warm-start seed (a subset stated, the rest left to the solver) -- see assignments. Assignment ids and employee ids refer to the expanded problem this solution belongs to. Standalone: this file does not reference any other schema. Symbols in square brackets refer to MathematicalDefinition7.

problemId.description: metadata.problemId of the problem this solves.

status.description: A 'feasible' or 'timeout' solution may still be worth warm-starting from; 'infeasible' and 'error' carry no assignments.

objectiveValues.description: Reported objective components, for comparing phases and runs.

goal.description: e.g. 'minimize_shortages' (ObjectiveFunction1, sum of z_dts), 'competency_priority_weight' (ObjectiveFunction2 -- the total priority weight of the assigned competency/level combinations, derived from demand.priorityOrder), 'preferable_days_off_worked' (ObjectiveFunction3, sum of x'_wd).

assignments.description: One entry per employee. A worker-day is SEEDED when it names a non-null assignmentId. As a partial warm-start seed, only seeded days constrain the solver: a null assignmentId (not working) and an omitted day are both OPEN -- the solver decides them. A full solution simply states every worker-day. A seeded day is a SOFT starting point (the solver may change it) unless locked = true makes it a HARD pin.

assignmentId.description: The chosen assignment [the h with x_wdh = 1], which must be one of this worker-day's assignmentIds in the expanded problem. null = not working. A non-null value is the SEED for this day; null is an open day in the seed role.

locked.description: true = a HARD pre-commitment: the solver must keep this exact assignment (the solution-side twin of the expanded problem's availability.days[].forced). Requires a non-null assignmentId. Absent/false = a SOFT seed the solver may change. Whether the solver penalises changing a soft seed is a solve-directive, not enforced here (see FUTURE.md).

workedPreferableDayOff.description: True when this day was the worker's preferable day-off [D_wk] and was scheduled anyway [x'_wd = 1]. Surfaced because it is what ObjectiveFunction3 penalises.

competencyPerSlot.description: Optional detail: which competency the worker served in each covered timeslot [y_wdts]. Omit when only the daily assignment matters.

shortfalls.description: Where coverage fell below the desired minimum [z_dts > 0]. There is no hard coverage constraint -- alpha_dts is the number of workers DESIRED and is pursued only through ObjectiveFunction1 -- so a perfectly feasible solution can still report shortfalls. This is the KPI surface for that.

minutes.description: Minutes from the start of the scheduling day (00:00). Values at or past 1440 express times after midnight, so a night shift 22:00-06:30 is 1320-1830 with no ambiguity.
